items.title: Screening
items.objective: Ensures candidates for employment and contractors are screened in accordance with relevant laws, regulations and ethical considerations proportionate to business requirements and information accessed.
items.whyItExists: Background checks help verify identity, integrity and suitability before granting access to information and facilities. Appropriate screening reduces the risk of insider threats, fraud and misuse of privileged access.
items.riskAddressed: Engaging individuals who pose unacceptable security, fraud or compliance risks due to unverified background or suitability.
items.implementationGuidance: Define screening requirements based on role sensitivity, access level and legal constraints, including identity verification, right to work, employment history and, where permitted and appropriate, criminal or credit checks. Apply consistent procedures through HR and onboarding, document results securely, and repeat or update checks when roles change significantly. Ensure contractors and third-party personnel meet equivalent requirements through contractual obligations.
evidenceExamples: Records of re-screening for role changes
items.auditTesting: Review screening procedures and sample joiners or contractors in sensitive roles to confirm required checks were completed, documented and approved before access was granted where applicable.
interviewQuestions: What screening is required for privileged or sensitive roles?
How do you ensure contractors meet screening expectations?
When are screening checks repeated?
items.scenario: A company granting administrators access to financial systems required identity verification and employment history checks before account provisioning, reducing risk from unsuitable hires in high-trust roles.

items.title: Terms and conditions of employment
items.objective: Ensures employment and contractual agreements state personnel and organisational responsibilities for information security.
items.whyItExists: Clear contractual terms set expectations for protecting information, complying with policies and handling breaches. They provide a basis for accountability during and after employment or engagement.
items.riskAddressed: Unclear security responsibilities leading to policy violations, weak accountability or disputes after incidents.
items.implementationGuidance: Include information security responsibilities in employment contracts and contractor agreements, covering confidentiality, acceptable use, compliance with policies, reporting obligations, intellectual property and consequences of violations. Ensure terms remain effective after termination where needed, such as confidentiality obligations. Communicate terms during onboarding and obtain acknowledgement; review templates when legal or policy requirements change.
evidenceExamples: Updated contract clauses after policy changes
items.auditTesting: Sample personnel records to confirm agreements include relevant security responsibilities and were acknowledged. Verify confidentiality and other obligations extend beyond termination where appropriate.
commonGaps: No acknowledgement or communication of obligations
interviewQuestions: Where are information security responsibilities stated for employees and contractors?
How are changes to security obligations communicated?
What obligations remain after employment ends?
items.scenario: An organisation updated contractor agreements to include incident reporting and data handling duties, ensuring external developers understood responsibilities before receiving repository access.

items.title: Information security awareness, education and training
items.objective: Ensures personnel and relevant interested parties receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training.
items.whyItExists: People are a critical part of security controls. Awareness and training help individuals recognise risks, follow policies and respond correctly to threats such as phishing, data mishandling and incident reporting needs.
items.riskAddressed: Human error and weak security behaviour due to lack of knowledge or outdated guidance.
items.implementationGuidance: Provide role-appropriate awareness and training at onboarding and at regular intervals, covering relevant policies, threats, reporting procedures and secure practices. Tailor content for specialised roles such as developers, administrators and incident responders. Track participation, assess effectiveness through feedback, exercises or metrics, and update materials based on incidents, emerging threats and organisational changes.
evidenceExamples: Phishing or exercise results and metrics
Updates based on incidents or threat trends
items.auditTesting: Review the training programme and sample records to confirm relevant personnel completed required awareness or role-based training. Evaluate whether effectiveness is measured and content is current.
commonGaps: Generic content not tailored to roles
No tracking of completion or effectiveness
interviewQuestions: How do you ensure staff know how to report a security incident?
What specialised training do privileged users receive?
How do you measure whether awareness activities are effective?
items.scenario: After phishing simulations showed repeated failures in one department, targeted training and reporting reminders were provided, improving reporting rates and reducing clicks in subsequent exercises.

items.title: Disciplinary process
items.objective: Ensures a formal and communicated disciplinary process is in place to take action against personnel and other relevant parties who commit information security policy violations.
items.whyItExists: A defined disciplinary process supports accountability and deterrence. It ensures violations are handled consistently, fairly and in line with legal and contractual requirements.
items.riskAddressed: Inconsistent or ineffective handling of security violations, reducing accountability and allowing repeated misconduct.
items.implementationGuidance: Document and communicate a disciplinary process for information security breaches, integrated with HR policies and applicable laws. Define examples of violations, investigation steps, evidence requirements, possible sanctions and escalation paths. Apply the process consistently, coordinate with legal and management as needed, and use outcomes to inform awareness or control improvements where appropriate.
items.auditTesting: Verify a disciplinary process exists, is communicated and aligns with legal requirements. Review sampled cases or process readiness to confirm violations can be investigated and addressed consistently.
commonGaps: No defined process for security violations
interviewQuestions: What happens when someone violates an information security policy?
How do you ensure disciplinary actions are fair and consistent?
Who is involved in investigating serious violations?
items.scenario: A clear disciplinary procedure helped management respond consistently when an employee shared restricted data externally, supporting investigation, corrective action and reinforcement of policy expectations.

items.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
items.objective: Ensures information security responsibilities and duties that remain valid after termination or change of employment are defined, communicated and enforced.
items.whyItExists: Access needs and responsibilities change when people leave or move roles. Failure to manage these changes can leave former personnel with access or unclear obligations regarding confidentiality and asset return.
items.riskAddressed: Retained access, unreturned assets or continued handling of sensitive information after role change or termination.
items.implementationGuidance: Define post-employment and role-change responsibilities in policies and agreements, including confidentiality, intellectual property, return of assets and ongoing cooperation where required. Coordinate HR, IT and managers to update access rights promptly, recover assets, transfer ownership of information and remind individuals of continuing obligations. Document completion of offboarding or transfer steps.
evidenceExamples: Access removal and asset return records
items.auditTesting: Sample leavers and role changes to confirm access was adjusted promptly, assets returned, responsibilities communicated and records completed. Verify continuing obligations are documented.
commonGaps: Access not removed promptly after departure
Assets or data ownership not transferred
interviewQuestions: How quickly is access removed when someone leaves or changes roles?
What continuing obligations apply after termination?
How do you confirm all assets have been returned?
items.scenario: When an administrator moved to a non-technical role, timely access review removed privileged accounts while HR and the manager confirmed ongoing confidentiality duties and transferred system ownership.

items.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
items.objective: Ensures confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting information protection needs are identified, documented, regularly reviewed and signed by relevant parties.
items.whyItExists: Confidentiality agreements formalise expectations for protecting sensitive information shared with employees, contractors and external parties. They support legal and contractual protection but must be appropriate and maintained.
items.riskAddressed: Unauthorised disclosure of sensitive information due to unclear or absent confidentiality obligations.
items.implementationGuidance: Identify situations requiring confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements based on information sensitivity and relationships. Use approved templates covering scope, permitted use, handling requirements, duration and post-termination obligations. Obtain signatures before granting access to confidential information, store agreements securely and review them periodically or when relationships change.
evidenceExamples: Register of agreements and review dates
items.auditTesting: Sample relationships involving confidential information and verify appropriate agreements are in place, signed, current and aligned with the information shared.
commonGaps: No NDA where sensitive information is shared
Generic agreements not suited to the context
interviewQuestions: When is an NDA required for staff or external parties?
How do you track NDA expiry or review dates?
What confidential information is covered by this agreement?
items.scenario: Before sharing product designs with a prospective supplier, procurement obtained a signed NDA defining permitted use and return of materials, reducing risk of unauthorised disclosure during evaluation.

items.title: Remote working
items.objective: Ensures security measures are implemented when personnel work remotely to protect information accessed, processed or stored outside the organisation’s premises.
items.whyItExists: Remote working changes the physical and network environment, increasing exposure to theft, unauthorised viewing, insecure networks and unmanaged devices. Defined controls help maintain protection outside traditional offices.
items.riskAddressed: Compromise or loss of information and systems used in remote working environments.
items.implementationGuidance: Define remote working requirements covering approved devices, secure connectivity, authentication, physical protection, handling of sensitive information, use of public networks and reporting of incidents. Provide guidance and tools such as VPN, endpoint protection and secure collaboration, and ensure access is based on business need. Assess risks for different remote scenarios and monitor compliance with technical and procedural controls.
evidenceExamples: Approved device and remote access configurations
User awareness materials for remote work
items.auditTesting: Review remote working controls and sample users to confirm secure access methods, device protections and policy requirements are applied. Verify incident reporting and support processes are available to remote staff.
commonGaps: Use of unmanaged devices without safeguards
Sensitive work performed over insecure networks
No guidance on physical privacy or device protection
interviewQuestions: What devices and connections are approved for remote work?
How is sensitive information protected in home or public environments?
How do remote workers report suspected incidents?
items.scenario: A company enabled secure remote access with MFA, device encryption and guidance on avoiding public Wi-Fi for sensitive tasks, allowing staff to work remotely while maintaining baseline protections.

items.title: Information security event reporting
items.objective: Ensures personnel are aware of and able to report observed or suspected information security events through appropriate channels in a timely manner.
items.whyItExists: Early reporting enables rapid assessment and response, limiting impact. If reporting channels are unclear or staff fear blame, events may go unreported until they become major incidents.
items.riskAddressed: Delayed detection and response because security events are not reported promptly or to the correct team.
items.implementationGuidance: Provide clear, accessible reporting channels for suspected events such as phishing, malware, lost devices, data leaks or policy violations. Communicate what constitutes an event, how to report, and what information to include, emphasising timely reporting without fear of inappropriate blame. Ensure reports are acknowledged, triaged and fed into incident management processes, and reinforce reporting through awareness activities.
items.responsibleDepartment: All Personnel / Security Operations / Service Desk
evidenceExamples: Event reporting procedures and contact channels
items.auditTesting: Verify reporting mechanisms are documented and available to all relevant personnel. Sample reported events to confirm they were received, acknowledged and routed for assessment promptly.
commonGaps: Reporting channels unclear or hard to find
Staff unsure what should be reported
interviewQuestions: How would an employee report a suspected phishing email?
What happens after an event is reported?
How do you encourage timely reporting?
items.scenario: A simplified ‘report phishing’ button and awareness reminders increased early reports of suspicious emails, allowing the security team to block malicious senders before widespread compromise.
